items.title: The layout changed slightly since your SK02 drawing
items.detail: The lounge wall moved 0.88 m east to line up with the house, the pool moved 0.5 m east, and the lounge now runs out to the old garden bed. The 3D model and drawings show it all.

items.title: East fence past the pillar
items.detail: Can the fence run straight past the east face of the pavilion pillar (so the pillar's inside the pool area), then along the deck edge?

images.caption: The fence stepping past the pillar

items.title: Kitchen sliding door
items.detail: Our quote from the builder includes a security door for it, permanently fixed shut since it opens into the pool area. Does it need to be in the drawings?

items.title: North fence moved north
items.detail: About 1.5 m further north than SK02, with the play area moved north too so it stays clear.

items.title: West boundary fence
items.detail: Doesn't need to be in the drawings. We're organising it ourselves, once we've talked to our neighbour.

items.title: Timber deck: how does it finish at the edges?
items.detail: We're not sure how the timber deck should finish. In the 3D model it runs right out to the edges. But if it has to sit on timber bearers, the limestone walls might need a cap round the edge like the sunken fire pit lounge, with the timber framed inside it. If so, the narrow strip along the east fence is probably too thin for timber, so the timber would stop at the spa deck, level with the lounge's south wall. What do you reckon?

images.caption: Alternative: capped edge, timber stops at the spa deck

items.title: Pump room: will it all fit?
items.detail: Will everything fit in there, with enough ventilation? That's the pool and spa pumps and filter now, plus pool heating and spa heating equipment later, all reached through the doors.

images.caption: The pump room under the spa deck

items.title: Roof sheeting changed to Stratco Smartspan
items.detail: The roof is only 2 degrees and Custom Orb needs at least 5, so the builder's swapped it for Stratco Smartspan. Downlights in the ceiling too.

items.title: One post at the roof corner
items.detail: A single post at the south-west corner, sitting on the lounge wall with a pier as its footing. Can the wall take it?

images.caption: The corner post on the lounge wall

items.title: Coping and capping: where do we actually need it?
items.detail: We think we'll need coping round the pool (400 x 400 aggregate, square or drop edge). But do we need capping anywhere else, like round the sunken fire pit lounge or along the wall facing the canal? Could it just be aggregate right to the edge there?

images.caption: Pool coping and the lounge wall cap, close up

items.title: Aggregate: TBD
items.detail: We haven't picked the exact aggregate yet, for the paving or the coping.

items.title: Below ground pool roller
items.detail: We'd like one at the deep end, but we suspect it's too narrow there (only about 0.41 m of paving between the coping and the wall cap at the tight corner, plus the wall's footing). If it's not possible, we'll need to discuss.

items.title: Lighting in the sunken lounge
items.detail: What's required on the drawings for the lighting we'd like in the sunken fire pit lounge?
